evidence.detail: Iter-4 input re-run: `/kiwi-wave-master ROADMAP_ITEM=RM-4`, no PRD path, RM-4 Actual Start '-', Targets '-', Requirements '-'. AC-1 (docs/spec/60.workflow-release.srs.md:15710) now places the single update_roadmap_item call 'at the moment the run commits its work graph and writes the run's first journal line (FR-FLOW-222 AC-1)', and branches on 'the committed work graph's `scope`'. FR-FLOW-222 AC-1 (:15439) records graph {path, digest} on the run's first journal line, and FR-FLOW-212 AC-1 (:14795) makes committing waves.json the last step after kiwi-prd, /kiwi-srs, impact analysis, wave propose and field filling, with any narrowing (AC-4, :14798) settled before that commit. So scope exists when the call is made: RM-4 gets Actual Start = run start date and Targets = product target (scope target) or Requirements = scope.requirements (narrowed run). AC-3 (:15712) still allows exactly that call; redecomposition (FR-FLOW-222 AC-1 'redecompose' line) is not the first journal line, so no second call. Title (:15677) and statement (:15694) say the same point ('when the run commits its work graph').

findings.description: The call point of AC-1 is now the work-graph commit (first journal line), where the scope it branches on exists.
